$comment: Cross-client parity matrix. Both runners read this file verbatim and configure through the same ordered calls, so neither can drift from the other. Base parameters are buckley_case_a from src/lib/ressim/src/tests/buckley.rs. `strict` cases must agree to 1e-9; non-strict ones are known to diverge across targets and report the gap instead of failing -- see the FIM note in docs/ARCHITECTURE_SPLIT_PLAN_2026-09-19.md.

cases.why: The original fixture. Three steps leaves the front mid-grid; a fully swept or static field would agree without proving much.

The same case on the implicit solver. NOT strict: wasm32 and x86-64 substep it differently -- 4 substeps against 18 on the very first day -- so their trajectories are not comparable at 1e-9. Kept, and reported on every run, so the divergence stays measured rather than forgotten.
Mobility ratio is the axis the catalog's sensitivities vary most. A favourable displacement moves the front differently and exercises the relperm path at different saturations.
Adverse mobility on the implicit solver; same cross-target substepping difference. Non-strict for the same reason as buckley-fim.

A different cell count changes array sizes across the boundary, and grid refinement is a numerics sensitivity in its own right. Short step because 12 highly permeable cells sweep in well under a day, and parity measured on a uniform field proves nothing (front lands at 5 of 12).
